question: Should iOS intentionally replace its established reconnect-progress-first behavior with a sticky same-target error as the primary status while a retry is running?
rationale: Current main has a test encoding reconnect progress as the expected state, while this PR deliberately prioritizes diagnostic readability; the permanent UX and interaction contract requires an iOS owner decision.

options.title: Scoped sticky error
options.body: Keep the same-target error visible, but add explicit busy state, disable actions, and let setup, target changes, and newer preflight failures replace it.

options.title: Reconnect progress first
options.body: Preserve the current primary reconnect status and expose the previous error through secondary details or history.

options.title: Refactor state model first
options.body: Pause this PR until gateway presentation state is explicitly modeled by target, attempt, and owner rather than precedence checks.

recommendation.title: Scoped sticky error
recommendation.body: Keep the same-target error visible, but add explicit busy state, disable actions, and let setup, target changes, and newer preflight failures replace it.

likelyOwner.reason: The maintainer-routed PR and recent iOS gateway work make steipete the best available owner for the intended reconnect UX contract.
